full_judgment: 10. Mr Sarder Abul Hossain, learned Advocate on the other hand appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that the Joint District Judge upon proper appreciation of evidence has rightly passed the judgment. He draws our attention to RS record 487 and submits that the RS record has got its presumptive value and defendants could not dislodge such presumption by any convincing evidence. The Joint District Judge upon perusal of Exhibits-3-9 has correctly found that the plaintiffs are entitled to a decree in part which may not be interfered with by this Court. The claim of the defendants relying upon two nadabi documents does not deserve any consideration because those do not confer any title. He laid much emphasis on the statement of DW 1 made in cross and submits that according to the admission of DW 1 the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 is not binding upon the plaintiffs and plaintiffs have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land. He referring to the deposition of DW 1 submits that the Joint District Judge has passed the judgment upon due consideration of materials on record and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. In course of hearing Mr Hossain filed an application for amendment of the plaint on 15-3-2023 and on 30-3-2023 filed another application for production of additional evidence. In support of those applications he submits that at the time of hearing of this appeal plaintiffs have come to know some important facts and documents with regard to their title which are very much necessary for proper adjudication of the dispute and unless those are considered and allowed the respondents shall suffer irreparable loss and injury.
